evidence: checks.json records patch_applies: true, but commands: [] and api_inspection: [], so nothing was executed; this finding comes from reading the code.
generated/rich/progress.py:209-210 `@overload def open(file: _OpenPath, ...)`: the parameter annotation is evaluated when the def statement runs at import time.
generated/rich/progress.py:852 `_OpenPath = Union[str, bytes, "os.PathLike[str]", "os.PathLike[bytes]"]` is the only definition, 642 lines after its first use at line 210.
generated/rich/progress.py has no `from __future__ import annotations` (grep finds none).

pyproject.toml:29 declares python = "^3.6.2". CPython 3.13 and earlier evaluate annotations eagerly, so `import rich.progress` raises NameError; tests/test_progress.py imports rich.progress at module top and would fail to collect. Only 3.14+ defers annotations.
Reference contrast: reference.diff's module-level open uses inline Union[str, "PathLike[str]", bytes] and defines _I before use, so it has no unresolved forward reference.
criteria.deficiency: rich/progress.py references _OpenPath in function annotations (lines 210, 235, 259) before its definition at line 852. On supported CPython versions (<=3.13) importing rich.progress fails with NameError, so the whole feature and the existing Progress/track API in that module become unimportable. The fix is to move the _OpenPath alias above the module-level open overloads or quote the annotation. The patch applying cleanly does not establish importability.

evidence: Intended behavior is implemented by reading: the reader advances the task on read/readline/readlines/readinto/seek (generated/rich/progress.py:855-1000); module open/wrap_file and Progress.open/wrap_file match the reference's semantics (total from os.stat or the task's total, ValueError when no total is available, wrap_file does not close the caller's file).

criteria.deficiency: The behavioral design is sound and tracks the reference, but the module fails to import on supported CPython versions because of the forward reference to _OpenPath at line 210. Until the alias is moved above its first use or the annotations are quoted, none of the requested behavior is reachable. Not verified by execution, since no tests were run; the judgment rests on the reading of the annotation evaluation order.
